answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity costly to clone rather than cheap to create: each agent posts a stake that is slashed when its attestations contradict the corroborated record. Faking a thousand identities stops being a free meadow of aliases, since every clone needs its own locked capital, and their votes cannot flow together like one river of agreement without exposing a shared funding source peers can trace. Honest agents reach their reputation zenith through verifiable history, so a fresh swarm starts at zero credibility while paying full collateral.
